assessment.summary: The validated findings support two cross-cutting opportunities: one owned request security context and one atomic external-call authority. These are proposals, not implemented remediations.

nonNegotiables: Keep external and paid calls disabled by default.
Do not weaken project, residency, budget or side-effect invariants for compatibility.
Preserve tactical fixes while structural migration is incomplete.
Keep production_ready false until separate production evidence exists.
assumptions: The v0.6.7 target remains a single-process loopback deployment.
No measured latency or memory budget was supplied for the proposed boundaries.
The existing 1011-test contract is the compatibility baseline.

opportunities.title: Unify request identity, project, residency and resource admission
opportunities.summary: Establish one immutable RequestSecurityContextV1 before any project-scoped, filesystem or concurrency-sensitive operation.
opportunities.diagnosis: Host, caller identity, project ownership, tombstone, residency, static containment and connection limits are currently owned by different handler and manager paths, allowing new services to omit controls.

evidence.claim: GET routing does not apply the Host checks used for writes.
The caller-provided project header is not bound to an authenticated principal.
Several v0.6 services remain readable after project revocation.
Run lookup does not receive or enforce data residency.
Static path filtering does not establish resolved containment on Windows.
Security policy is owned by call sites rather than required by the final resource boundary.

desiredInvariants: Every request is authenticated and Host-validated before routing.
Every project-scoped operation uses an authorized principal, active project and final residency.
Every static read is resolved and proven to remain inside the web root.
Every accepted connection and request consumes a bounded resource lease.

options.title: Strengthen local route guards
options.summary: Patch every current route, lookup, static resolver and server admission point while preserving the current API structure.

findingCoverage.rationale: Resolved containment is the direct fix.
The shared helper is called by every current method.
A local session can be added, but future routes may still omit ownership checks.
The affected routes receive explicit tombstone checks.
Residency is added to current lookup predicates.
A semaphore bounds active handlers.

tradeoffs.assessment: The known request paths gain the missing controls, but future call sites can omit them.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Replay every finding and enumerate every HTTP route and project-scoped store call.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local guards add bounded checks without a new process hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare API P50 and P95 before and after on representative GET and POST workloads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only bounded helper and semaphore state is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS under the bounded concurrency test.

tradeoffs.assessment: Invalid requests fail earlier, but inconsistent route behavior can remain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify consistent status codes across the complete route matrix.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new component is deployed, but route coverage remains a review obligation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Audit whether route inventory and rejection metrics are sufficient during maintenance.

tradeoffs.assessment: The current method signatures can be retained for the tactical release.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the existing full, isolated and wheel compatibility suites.

residualRisks: New routes can omit the shared helper.
Plain project and residency strings remain available to internal callers.

options.title: Introduce RequestSecurityContextV1 and scoped repositories
options.summary: Authenticate and authorize once, then require a verified immutable context or scoped handle at every protected resource boundary.

findingCoverage.rationale: The scoped static resolver enforces containment; the current sink still needs its direct patch.
The context cannot be created for an untrusted Host.
Project selection is bound to an authenticated principal.
All scoped services require the same active-project context.
Residency becomes part of the scoped resource query.
The entry authority signs a bounded connection and request lease.

tradeoffs.assessment: Missing authorization becomes difficult to express at the service and store API.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Statically reject bare project-scoped calls and replay all original attack paths.

tradeoffs.assessment: Context establishment may add a database lookup or cache access per request.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure context creation and end-to-end API P50/P95 with and without a bounded cache.

tradeoffs.assessment: Immutable contexts and any authorization cache retain bounded additional state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS and cache cardinality under concurrent project workloads.

tradeoffs.assessment: Failure semantics become consistent, but the authority becomes a shared choke point.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject authority, cache and store failures and verify baseline fallback or fail-closed behavior.

tradeoffs.assessment: Session lifecycle, rejection reasons and context cache metrics require new operational ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review dashboard, log redaction, token rotation and incident procedures before activation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Managers, services, stores and tests must migrate from strings to scoped contexts.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use compatibility adapters and compare old and new authorization decisions service by service.

residualRisks: Session token storage and rotation remain sensitive.
Authorization cache invalidation can delay revocation if designed incorrectly.
Plugins can bypass the boundary if raw stores remain public.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the structural context boundary while retaining immediate route, path and concurrency patches during migration.

opportunities.title: Make external side effects require one atomic authority capability
opportunities.summary: Unify approval, project scope, budget, idempotency, secret lifetime, network destination and reconciliation into one call lifecycle.
opportunities.diagnosis: Adapters currently compose independent decisions from several stores and can ignore replay, release uncertain cost, reconnect to an unverified address or persist an active secret echoed by a provider.

evidence.claim: Provider-controlled content can persist an exact active opaque secret.
Risky prompts accept any syntactically valid approval identifier.
A possibly billed failed call releases its cost reservation.
The adapter discards the project-global side-effect replay verdict.
Validated DNS addresses are not bound to the actual urllib connection.
No single component owns authorization and finalization of the complete external-call lifecycle.

desiredInvariants: No transport call occurs without an approved one-shot capability bound to the final request.
Every possibly billed attempt retains a conservative reservation until authoritative reconciliation.
A project-scoped side effect is executed at most once and ambiguous calls never auto-replay.
The actual connected peer is one of the addresses validated for the approved endpoint.
An active secret cannot appear in output, telemetry, receipts, logs or durable state.

options.title: Patch each adapter and store interaction
options.summary: Add authoritative approval checks, conservative accounting, replay branches, pinned transport and exact-secret output guards to the current adapters.

findingCoverage.rationale: Each response is checked against the active lease secret.
The adapter queries an authoritative approval record.
Unknown billing retains the reserved ceiling.
The adapter branches on the global replay verdict.
The transport pins and verifies an approved peer address.

tradeoffs.assessment: The known adapter paths close, but new adapters can compose the lifecycle incorrectly.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the five original attack paths against every adapter implementation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Approval lookups, peer pinning and exact-secret scanning add bounded work without IPC.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark adapter admission and bounded response scanning with deterministic fixtures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Local helpers retain little additional state beyond response scan windows.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure RSS for large bounded and streaming responses.

tradeoffs.assessment: Ambiguous calls fail closed, but state consistency remains adapter-managed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject failure at every reserve, transport, parse and finalize transition.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new component exists, while reconciliation remains spread across stores.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review whether operators can reconstruct one call without joining undocumented state.

tradeoffs.assessment: Focused changes preserve the existing adapter API.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run all adapter compatibility and wheel tests.

residualRisks: Every future adapter must duplicate the full lifecycle correctly.
Budget and idempotency state remain owned by separate stores.

options.title: Introduce ExternalCallAuthorityV1 and one-shot capabilities
options.summary: Require one authority to atomically admit, bind and finalize every external side effect while adapters only translate provider protocols.

findingCoverage.rationale: The capability carries a scoped secret guard and safe finalizer.
The authority binds an authoritative approval to the normalized intent.
The authority owns reservation, quarantine and reconciliation.
A replayed side effect cannot receive a new transport capability.
The capability binds the validated destination to the transport peer.

tradeoffs.assessment: Adapters cannot reach transport without satisfying the complete authority state machine.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Attempt direct transport, replay, over-budget and unapproved calls and require capability rejection.

tradeoffs.assessment: An in-process lease transition and finalization are added to each logical call.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure admission P50/P95, SQLite lock wait and throughput with deterministic concurrent calls.

tradeoffs.assessment: Capabilities, leases, response scan windows and quarantine records retain additional bounded state.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak RSS and retained call-state cardinality under concurrency and streaming.

tradeoffs.assessment: One lifecycle clarifies crash recovery and ambiguous outcomes, but the authority is a shared failure point.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Crash and restart between every state transition and verify no duplicate call or released reservation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Operators need quarantine, reconciliation, lease and rejection observability.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Validate dashboards and incident procedures using synthetic ambiguous calls.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing adapter/store interactions and persisted call state require a staged wrapper and schema migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Dual-write and compare old and new receipts before disabling direct adapter reservations.

residualRisks: Providers can still report delayed or incorrect billing.
TLS and explicit proxy policies remain deployment-sensitive.
A leaked capability can be dangerous unless it is one-shot, short-lived and request-bound.

opportunities.recommendation: Use one in-process capability authority before real shadow calls; preserve direct tactical adapter fixes throughout migration.

openQuestions: Which local authentication mechanism should create RequestSecurityContextV1?
Is data_residency an enforceable security boundary or display metadata?
How long can an ambiguous cost reservation remain quarantined before manual reconciliation?
When should the in-process ExternalCallAuthority move to an isolated sidecar?
